about: The managing partner of the law firm Ford, Dean & Rotundo, P.A., in North Miami Beach, Florida, William A. Dean is a seasoned attorney of 25 years representing victims of abuse and neglect in nursing homes and assisted living facilities. Nationally renowned in this area of law, he helps patients who have been wronged and their families seek justice and monetary compensation for the ill treatment they received.

Board certified in civil trial advocacy by The Florida Bar and the National Board of Trial Advocacy, Mr. Dean has obtained over $100 million in verdicts and settlements. He deeply cares about his clients, which is why he works hard to pursue every opportunity to see to it that they get the compensation they need to start fresh and move on from the past.

Mr. Dean graduated from Union College in 1992 with a Bachelor of Arts degree in history. He then attended New York Law School and received his Juris Doctor degree, cum laude, in 1997. During his time in law school, he was inducted into the Order of the Bannisters and won Best Oralist and Best Petitioner’s Brief. He was also a finalist at the John J. Gibbons National Criminal Procedure Moot Court Competition.

Mr. Dean is licensed to practice in Florida, New York, Georgia and Massachusetts and is admitted to practice before the United States District Courts for the Southern, Middle and Northern Districts of Florida, as well as before the Supreme Court of the United States.

Before entering private practice, Mr. Dean was an attorney at the Miami-Dade State Attorney’s Office, where he founded the Special Operations – Special Narcotics Unit, investigated violent felony crimes of organized drug traffickers and oversaw the prosecution as well. With his firsthand insight into the Florida judicial system, he can help navigate through the tough legal hurdles the state has in place.
Mr. Dean has received many honors for his achievements during the span of his career, including:

He is professionally affiliated with various prestigious legal organizations, including the Florida Justice Association, the American Association for Justice, the Miami-Dade County League of Prosecutors, the Association of Trial Lawyers of America and the Southern Trial Lawyers Association.
